rationale: The book identifies righteousness as right-living: God's own ways as the measure of right, and for those under His authority, the doing of His commandments — with grace answering how righteousness is received (forgiveness of wrongs, reception of faithful obedience) rather than converting righteousness into a bare status. This identification is directly and repeatedly stated by the supplied texts in definitional form: Deuteronomy 6:25 ('it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments'), Psalm 119:172 ('all thy commandments are righteousness'), 1 John 3:7 ('he that doeth righteousness is righteous'), and for God Himself Deuteronomy 32:4 and Psalm 145:17 (righteous 'in all his ways... in all his works'). The strongest rival — forensic/imputed righteousness as a legal status credited apart from any doing — must either bracket these definitional verses as a secondary 'ethical' sense or read them against their plain wording, whereas the book's reading unifies the whole corpus with one referent. On the forensic proof texts themselves, the book gives a coherent, textually grounded account: Romans 4:4 defines the excluded 'work' as wage-labor creating debt (a reading already established as an accepted prior finding on 'works'), Luke 17:7-10 shows obedience is not wage-labor and earns no debt, Romans 4:7-8 states the imputation mechanism as forgiveness and covering (not renaming wrong right), Hebrews 11:8 shows Abraham's counted faith was enacted in obedience (matching the accepted prior findings on faith and belief), and Philippians 3:9's contrast is source and claim ('mine own' vs. 'of God by faith'), with Paul immediately commanding walking by the rule (3:16). The chapter also supplies a decisive lexical detail the common reading obscures: Revelation 19:8's fine linen is dikaiōmata — plural righteous acts — 'given unto her' yet done by her, exactly the book's granted-then-worn structure. No supplied text is better explained by the status-only counter; several supplied texts are inexplicable under it without introducing an unannounced second sense of the word.
book_core_identification: Righteousness is right-living — conformity to God's ways as the measure of right: God is righteous in that all His ways and works are right, and for creatures under His authority righteousness is the doing of His commandments; it is given and reckoned by grace (through forgiveness of wrong and reception of faithful obedience), but the gift never redefines righteousness as anything other than right-living.
book_secondary_elaborations: Romans 4 excludes wage-work that would put God in debt, not obedience; work-for-wages and obedience-to-command are distinct relations (Luke 17:7-10).
Even complete obedience earns no wage because the servant has only done his duty; grace explains reception, not substance.
The garment/robe imagery (Rev 19:8 dikaiōmata; Isa 61:10; Zech 3:4) pictures righteousness as righteous acts granted, worn, defiled, and washed — 'the covenant worn.'
Isaiah 64:6's filthy rags indict the sin staining the doer, not the righteous act itself.
Philippians 3:9 contrasts source and claim (mine by debt vs. God's by faith), not right-living against lawlessness.
Imputation operates by forgiving iniquity and covering sin (Rom 4:7-8), not by renaming wrong-living right.
strongest_counter_interpretation: Righteousness, in its dominant theological (Pauline) sense, is a forensic status: God's righteousness credited (imputed) to the believer through faith in Christ apart from works. On this reading Romans 4:5-6 ('imputeth righteousness without works,' faith 'counted for righteousness' to one who 'worketh not') and Philippians 3:9 ('not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law') establish that saving righteousness is a declared standing, an alien righteousness received rather than lived; commandment-keeping texts like Deuteronomy 6:25 and 1 John 3:7 describe a distinct, secondary ethical sense (or the fruit of the status), not the term's core referent.
counter_core_identification: Righteousness is fundamentally a legal/relational status before God — right standing declared and credited by God on the basis of faith, categorically distinct from and prior to any right conduct.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that righteousness is in substance right-living: it holds that in the decisive justification texts the word names a credited standing that exists apart from — and is expressly contrasted with — anything the person does, so that a status-bearer is righteous even where right-living is absent; the book holds that righteousness never names anything other than right-living, only received by grace.
counter_case: Romans 4:5 — faith is counted for righteousness to 'him that worketh not,' and God 'justifieth the ungodly,' suggesting a declaration made prior to and apart from right-living.
Romans 4:6 — God 'imputeth righteousness without works,' read as crediting a status with no deed-content.
Philippians 3:9 — Paul renounces 'mine own righteousness, which is of the law' in favor of 'the righteousness which is of God by faith,' read as alien righteousness replacing law-keeping.
Isaiah 64:6 (invoked by the common view) — 'all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags,' read as disqualifying human right-doing as such.
The garment imagery (Isa 61:10) read as a covering bestowed over the sinner, symbolizing a status that requires no weaving of deeds.
book_explanatory_advantages: Explains the direct definitional texts without remainder: Deut 6:25 and Ps 119:172 define human righteousness as commandment-doing, and 1 John 3:7 explicitly warns against the deceit that one can be righteous without doing righteousness — the counter must demote these to a second sense of the word.
Provides a single sense covering both God and man: Deut 32:4 and Ps 145:17 locate God's righteousness in His ways and works (doing), which the status reading cannot apply to God at all.

Explains Romans 4 internally: v.4 itself defines the excluded category as wage-work creating debt, v.7-8 states the mechanism as forgiveness and covering — the book's account uses Paul's own definitions, and rests on the already-accepted prior finding that 'works' means wage-claimed deeds, not obedience.
Explains Luke 17:7-10, printed with the entry: obedience earns no wage and creates no debt, dissolving the alleged equivalence between 'not of works' and 'not of obedience.'
Explains why Abraham's counted faith is narrated as obedience (Heb 11:8), consistent with the accepted prior findings that faith and belief are constitutively obedient.

Explains the Greek of Rev 19:8 (dikaiōmata, righteous acts) and the granted-then-worn grammar ('it was given unto her that she should array herself'), which the status reading — built partly on the KJV's shortened 'righteousness of saints' — cannot accommodate.
Explains the defilement/washing/keeping texts (Rev 3:4; 16:15; Zech 3:4; Jude 23): a bare credited status cannot be soiled by conduct or kept by doing, but a garment of righteous acts can.
Accounts for Isaiah 64:6 in context: the whole line says 'we are all as an unclean thing,' locating the filth in the sinner staining the deed, not in right-doing as such.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Gives the most immediate surface reading of 'justifieth the ungodly' and 'imputeth righteousness without works' (Rom 4:5-6), where a declaration seems to precede any right-living.
Preserves a sharp works/faith antithesis without needing the wage-work vs. obedience distinction.
Reads Philippians 3:9 in line with the dominant Protestant tradition of alien righteousness.
Offers a simple account of why sinners can be called righteous at all: the status is Christ's, not theirs.
decisive_sources: Deuteronomy 6:25 — an explicit scriptural definition: 'it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments.'
1 John 3:7 — 'let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous,' an explicit canonical warning against the status-without-doing reading.
Deuteronomy 32:4 and Psalm 145:17 — God's righteousness located in His ways and works, requiring a doing-sense that also covers God.
Romans 4:4-8 read with Luke 17:7-10 — Paul's excluded 'work' is wage-labor creating debt; obedience creates no debt; imputation proceeds by forgiveness and covering.
Revelation 19:8 (dikaiōmata) — the wedding garment is righteous acts, given and put on, confirming 'granted, then worn.'
Accepted prior findings on works, faith, belief, and love, which jointly establish the wage-work/obedience distinction and the obedience-constitutive nature of counted faith.
unresolved_objections: The precise temporal mechanics of Romans 4:5 — God 'justifieth the ungodly' — still permit a reading in which a declarative verdict precedes any accumulated right-living; the book answers via forgiveness-plus-received-faithful-obedience, but the ordering question is not fully settled by the supplied texts.
Texts central to the imputation tradition but not adjudicated here (Rom 5:17-19; 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Cor 1:30) could be pressed for an alien-righteousness reading; the chapter does not treat them.

Whether Philippians 3:9's 'righteousness of God by faith' is exhaustively explained as 'source and claim' rather than also carrying a status component remains arguable, though this disputes mechanism rather than the core referent.
